reference.title: Quick reference
reference.lede: The cross-cutting material that does not belong to any one topic. This is the page to reopen the night before a test.
reference.summary: Articles, fractions, checks and balances, House and Senate, clauses, amendments

sections.title: The seven Articles
rows: The legislative branch. Structure of Congress, its enumerated powers, limits on Congress and on the states.
The executive branch. The presidency, its powers and duties, the Electoral College.
The judicial branch. The Supreme Court, the power to create lower courts, jurisdiction, treason.
Relations among the states. Full faith and credit, privileges and immunities, extradition, admission of new states.
The supremacy clause, national debts, oaths of office, and the ban on religious tests for office.
Ratification — the Constitution took effect once conventions in nine states approved it.
sections.note: Know the Article numbers. You are not expected to memorize section numbers — a question may cite one, but you will never be asked to supply it. Section numbers appear in the tables below only so you can find provisions quickly when you go back to the text.

sections.title: Checks and balances
rows: Bicameral — a bill must pass both chambers · Revenue bills must originate in the House · Neither chamber may adjourn more than three days without the other’s consent
Override a veto by two-thirds · Impeach and remove · Confirm or reject appointments · Ratify or reject treaties · Declare war · Control appropriations

Confirm or reject judicial nominees · Impeach and remove judges · Create lower courts and set their jurisdiction · Alter the size of the Supreme Court · Propose amendments to overturn constitutional rulings
Veto legislation · Call Congress into special session · Deliver the State of the Union and recommend measures
Judicial review — declare an act of Congress unconstitutional
Judicial review — declare an executive action unconstitutional
sections.note: Read across a row to see what that branch can do to the others. Read down a column to see what restrains that branch. Judges hold their seats during good behavior and their pay cannot be reduced, which insulates the judiciary from pressure by the other two.

sections.title: Clauses to know
rows: Lets Congress make laws needed to carry out its listed powers. The basis of implied powers.
Gives Congress power over commerce with foreign nations, among the states, and with tribes. Interstate, not intrastate.
Habeas corpus, ex post facto, bills of attainder
Limits on what Congress and the states may do to individuals.
Requires the president to see that the laws are faithfully executed.
Requires each state to honor the public acts, records, and judicial proceedings of other states.
Requires a state to return a person charged with a crime who has fled from another state.
Makes the Constitution, federal laws, and treaties the supreme law of the land.
Reserves to the states, or to the people, powers not delegated to the national government.

sections.title: Amendments that changed the original text
cols: What it did to the original text
rows: Abolished slavery, which ended the counting of enslaved persons under the three-fifths formula.

Defined citizenship for all persons born or naturalized in the United States, extending it to formerly enslaved people. Section 2 rewrote apportionment to count the whole number of persons in each state. Also added due process and equal protection.
Barred denial of the vote on account of race, color, or previous condition of servitude — the first constitutional limit on state authority over voter qualifications.
Allowed Congress to tax incomes without apportioning the tax among the states by population.
Replaced selection of senators by state legislatures with direct election by voters.
Limited the president to two elected terms, where the original text set no limit.
